- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < -0.30 for 3+ days), model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward recent highs.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3-day moving average of forecast before final output.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >3% from 14-day moving average of history, adjust forecast toward historical mean (not just recent trend).
- When sentiment turns from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per 3-day window.
